item.content:encoded: I disagree, the movement from North American to African animals felt like a nice bit of syncretic storyingtelling showing how folklore gets changed and adapted to new places.

item.content:encoded: I'm not too interested in this GOI, but the ending is good enough for me to upvote, even if it could be much shorter imo (like what Roget said).

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: This is pretty innovative. I share some of RTME's criticism of the writing on the notes, but it's not enough to pull me out.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I have a bit of a hang-up with notes in writing like someone speaks, because though this person clearly has a way of talking, I have a sincere doubt that anybody writes like this. However, I found the joke here funny, I found the interactions with various animals charming, and it won me over. So have your upvote.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: It’s a cute idea, but it would work far better if it was cut down to about half its length. The Leopard and Turtle were standouts but most of the others were just retreading the same basic interaction repeatedly. Also the folksy accent felt like it was laid on a bit too thick up front when describing the discovery and acquisition of the boot.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: This does a much better job establishing its own tone and identity than Legba Welcomes You. Mr. Nancy and Mr. Leopard's interactions are particularly amusing.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: This has gotta be one of my favorite articles that have come out of this GoI yet. It reads kinda like a back-alley children's book, and that's always a really good vibe. +1
